mechanism_narrative: The federal funds rate at its current low level (0.08%) is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as it reflects an accommodative monetary policy that supports equity valuations and reduces the risk-free rate, increasing the present value of future cash flows.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is at or below 0.1%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: The unemployment rate at its current high level (11.1%) is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as it signals a potential for monetary policy easing and economic stimulus, which supports equity markets.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when UNRATE is above 10%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.1% triggers a positive S&P 500 forward return signal over the next 5 trading days, as it reflects an immediate accommodative monetary policy that reduces the risk-free rate and increases the present value of equity cash flows.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 0.1%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts below 1000 thousand units trigger a negative S&P 500 forward return signal over the next 60 trading days, as it reflects a weakening housing market and potential economic slowdown, which increases risk aversion and reduces equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances when HOUST < 1000, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is at or below 0.1% and the unemployment rate is at or above 10%, it triggers a positive S&P 500 forward return signal over the next 20 trading days, as it reflects a combination of accommodative monetary policy and high labor market slack, which supports equity valuations through reduced risk-free rates and potential for fiscal stimulus.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS<=0.1% and UNRATE>=10%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts exceed 950 thousand units and industrial production exceeds 95 (2017=100), it triggers a positive S&P 500 forward return signal over the next 60 trading days, as it reflects a synchronized expansion in the housing market and industrial output, which signals strong economic growth and increased corporate earnings, supporting equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of instances when HOUST>950 and INDPRO>95, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 2.0%), the S&P 500 is predicted to produce negative forward returns over the next 5 trading days, as it reflects a contractionary monetary policy that increases the risk-free rate and reduces the present value of equity cash flows, while also signaling potential economic slowdown.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 2.0%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When private sector employment (PAYEMS) falls below 135,000 thousand persons, it triggers a negative S&P 500 forward return signal over the next 60 trading days, as it reflects a deteriorating labor market and potential economic contraction, which increases risk aversion and reduces equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances when PAYEMS < 135000, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
